description:
Deliver addressed peer messages only to live children in the same group. Best effort, nonblocking. Include the **parent** `send_minion_message` tool (not installed on children).

## Background

No durable mailbox, no exactly-once, no wait-for-reply, no parked sessions. Send returns immediately. Live recipient: steer/followUp at a child-safe boundary (may postpone idle). Terminal: recipient-terminal. Do not reroute through the parent. Peer messages do not start a parent turn.

Child send tools are bound closures from the inject issue. This issue owns delivery + the parent-facing send tool.

## Bounds (minions-local, not a rate-limit product)

- Max message body bytes (pick one number, test the boundary).
- Max in-memory queue depth per recipient (mailbox-full).
- In-process message id for inspection/tests only — not a durable mail log, not an exactly-once key.

No per-minute rate limiter. No depth beyond the queue cap. No glob/mail-server.

## Success criteria

- Same-group live delivery (child→child and parent→child).
- Cross-group, missing, terminal → closed reasons: recipient-terminal, invalid-recipient, group-not-open, mailbox-full.
- Child cannot forge sender identity.
- Peer-only send does not start a parent turn.

## Test plan

- Unit: ACL, identity from closure, body-size reject, queue-full reject.
- Integration: live vs disposed; parent send vs child send.
- Logging: in-process id, from, to, status, bytes, parent-turn-triggered=false for peer-only.

## Considerations

Peer chat can delay settlement. Halt is the escape. Mail vs settle is the sibling race issue.
